applicability.note: The SHAPE is as portable as anything this project holds: every elected office in the United States is created by a statute or a charter, and that instrument — not a canvass — is what says whether the office carries a party. It is also cheap, stable and citable: a canvass answers for ONE election and has to be re-read every cycle, while the statute answers for the office until the legislature changes it. Proved on A.R.S. 48-3708 and 48-3709 for the Central Arizona Water Conservation District, where four election-authority documents had failed to settle the same question. The limits are real and worth stating: a statute says what MUST happen and never what DID, so it can establish partisanship, apportionment and term but can never establish that a particular contest appeared on a particular ballot or who filed for it.

routes.title: an expiring term is a POSITION TO BE FILLED and never a ballot contest — check the county board's cancellation resolution before recording either a contest or an absence

applicability.note: A.R.S. 16-410 lets a county board of supervisors cancel any Title 15 or Title 48 district election where the people who filed are fewer than or equal to the positions, appoint them 'fully vested ... as if elected', and forbids the cancelled election from appearing on ANY ballot. So a seat can turn over on schedule while its contest exists in no ballot, no sample ballot and no canvass. THE SHAPE TRAVELS EVEN WHERE THE SECTION NUMBER DOES NOT: uncontested-election cancellation is common across states for school and special districts, and it is the standing explanation for the puzzle 'a term expires this year and we can find no contest'. Do not read that silence as our own retrieval failing, and do not read it as the government failing to hold an election. Read the county's own cancellation resolution. THE COROLLARY THAT BITES: an ABSENCE may not be recorded either, because a true absence now requires knowing an election was cancelled rather than merely not finding one.

outcomes.note: Reconciled the CAWCD 2020 disagreement and DISPROVED the standing inference on NH244 that four expiring Pima seats are therefore four 2026 ballot contests. routes.title: the agenda-vendor portal a district links its board agendas to — and the blanket robots disallow that governs BOTH of the big ones

applicability.note: THE SHAPE IS GENERAL AND IT IS A PERMISSION FACT, NOT A WALL. Two vendor hosts were read on 2026-08-27 and both publish a blanket disallow for every automated client: vailschooldistrict.community.highbond.com/robots.txt (23,479 bytes, 486 User-agent blocks, EXACTLY ONE 'User-agent: *' block carrying 'Disallow: /', and ZERO 'Allow:' directives anywhere in the file) and go.boarddocs.com/robots.txt (21,760 bytes, 'User-agent: * / Disallow: / / Crawl-delay: 1000'). Both were fetched successfully at rung 2, twice, with a bare curl client and with a browser user agent, so this is a READ RULE and not a transport failure — the CANNOT_TELL case of RULING 182 does not apply and must not be claimed here. routes.title: driving Legistar InSite's own Calendar.aspx date-range postback — the only complete enumeration of a tenant's sittings

applicability.note: THE MECHANICS, WRITTEN DOWN SO THE WALL NEVER COSTS A SECOND SESSION. (1) GET https://{tenant}.legistar.com/Calendar.aspx and keep EVERY form field it rendered. Read the rendered selection back out of ctl00_ContentPlaceHolder1_lstYears_Input to prove the filter took. The dropdown's own vocabulary is This/Next Week, Month, Year, All Years and every year back to 2013. (3) Parse rows on class="rgRow"/"rgAltRow" and key cells on their ASP.NET control-id suffixes (hypBody, lblTime, hypiCal, hypMeetingDetail, hypAgenda, hypAccessibleAgendaHTML, hypMinutes, hypAccessibleMinutesHTML) rather than on column position, which a tenant can reorder. routes.title: a reconciled denominator answers whether rows were LOST; it says nothing about whether enough was ASKED FOR

applicability.note: THE CORRECTION, AND IT IS AN ACCOUNTING LESSON RATHER THAN A RETRIEVAL ONE. 'fetched 16, normalized 16, drops accounted' is a strong, true statement about ONE ROUTE'S ANSWER: nothing between that source and the screen was dropped. It is not a statement about the body's calendar, and the two get confused because the reconciliation feels like a proof and there is nothing else in view to compare it against. THE FAILURE MODE, OBSERVED: a session read a per-source denominator that reconciled exactly, queried the primary API by hand over the same window, got the same answer, and recorded the snapshot as 'complete for the window' — then inferred from the API's silence a fact about the government (that it publishes September only as a recurring rule). Every measurement in that chain was correct; the inference was false, and the portal published all three sittings individually. THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT IS MISSING FROM A RECONCILED DENOMINATOR IS A SECOND ROUTE. Until a second independent route has been asked the same question, a reconciled count has a denominator of ONE ROUTE'S OPINION, and the honest sentence is 'this route returned N and nothing was lost', never 'there are N'. THE CHEAP SECOND ROUTE for a vendor-backed body is the vendor's own web UI (see vendor-api-and-vendor-web-ui-are-different-records); for a body's own site it is the sitemap. RULING 100 already says a partial that reconciles is still a wrong answer — this is that ruling meeting a real reconciliation and losing.

routes.title: 'born-digital' is a measurement, and an unverified one costs a later session a false absence

applicability.note: THE PORTABLE RULE. A PDF's class — born-digital with a text layer, versus a raster scan needing OCR — is the single fact that decides which extraction rung applies, and it is cheap to measure and expensive to assume. RECORD IT ONLY FROM AN ACTUAL EXTRACTION, and record the numbers: rows, pages, pagesWithText. A publisher very often runs TWO pipelines side by side, so the class travels with the DOCUMENT CLASS and never with the host: on www.azleg.gov the chaptered bill texts under /legtext/ are born-digital and the Governor's transmittal letters under /govlettr/ are scans, and they are two directories on the same server. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: an unverified 'born-digital' is inherited by every later jurisdiction as a reason to trust a text layer, and when the text layer returns nothing the next session is being asked to choose between 'the parser failed' and 'the document is empty' with a stale note nudging it toward the second. That is the ZERO_ROWS-as-empty-document defect arriving pre-argued. THE CHEAP CHECK: run the text layer on ONE document of the class and look at pagesWithText; if it is zero, look at the PDF's internals (/Font count, /Image count, filter names) and write down what you saw, not what you expected.

outcomes.note: Two document classes on one permitted host correctly classified — /legtext/ born-digital and EXTRACTED, /govlettr/ scanned and ZERO_ROWS — replacing one unmeasured claim that covered both.

routes.title: a byte grep over a born-digital PDF finds nothing on a document that says it plainly, and the nothing becomes a false absence

applicability.note: THE MISTAKE THIS PREVENTS IS MANUFACTURING A NAMED GAP OUT OF A BROKEN INSTRUMENT. A prior walk recorded that an enacted Arizona bill has NO PUBLISHED SIGNING DATE, on the evidence that grepping a chaptered version for approved|governor|filed returned nothing. The grep was run over the PDF's BYTES. A born-digital PDF stores its text inside FlateDecode content streams, so a byte grep cannot match ordinary words in it and returns nothing regardless of what the document says — the measurement was guaranteed to produce that answer before it was run. MEASURED CORRECTLY 2026-08-28: extract the text layer first, and every chaptered version at https://www.azleg.gov/legtext/57Leg/2R/laws/<NNNN>.pdf ends with its own enactment stamp — 'APPROVED BY THE GOVERNOR FEBRUARY 6, 2026. FILED IN THE OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY OF STATE FEBRUARY 6, 2026.' That is a signing date, published by the state, in the primary document, for every enacted bill. THE GENERAL RULE: NEVER grep, regex or string-search a PDF, a DOCX or any compressed container directly. Run the extraction layer and search ITS OUTPUT, and if the extraction returns nothing, that is a finding about the extraction. WHY THIS ONE IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG: it does not fail loudly. It produces a confident, specific, plausible-sounding absence — 'the state does not publish signing dates' — which is a false claim about a government, and it then hardens into a NAMED GAP that later sessions inherit and cite. A SECOND LESSON FROM THE SAME DOCUMENT: read the stamp's WORDING, not just its date. A bill reaches a chapter three ways — approved by the governor, becoming law without signature, or passage over a veto — so 'chaptered' proves ENACTMENT and never proves a SIGNATURE, and filing every chapter as 'signed' is its own false claim about a governmental act.

outcomes.note: The signing date for all 264 chaptered bills of 57leg/2r moved from 'no permitted machine-readable source' to a field read off each act's own stamp, together with the enactment ROUTE that says whether a signature happened at all.

routes.title: a Streamline-hosted special district publishes one URL per sitting, and its sitemap enumerates every one

applicability.note: THE SHAPE TRAVELS BECAUSE THE VENDOR DOES. Streamline publishes each sitting at a path of the form /<YYYY>-<MM>-<DD>-<body>-<slug>, so the DATE, the BODY and the meeting KIND are already separated in the URL before anything is parsed, and sitemap.xml lists them all. No API, no account, no pagination and no date-range control to defeat. Read 2026-08-29 on two tenants with byte-identical robots policy shape: www.coronafire.org (Corona de Tucson Fire District) yielded 115 dated sittings 2017-2026 and 5 directors with emails; www.sefd911.org (Sonoita-Elgin Fire District) yielded 70 dated sittings and 5 directors with seat, term, phone and email. Both robots.txt carry 'User-agent: * / Allow: /' with named disallows confined to SEO crawlers (SemrushBot, AhrefsBot, Sidetrade, PetalBot, MJ12bot). WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TWO FIRE DISTRICTS: Streamline's market is SPECIAL DISTRICTS, which is the thinnest governmental layer in this product in every state worked so far, and the layer least likely to appear in any directory. The route to test on a new special district is its sitemap BEFORE its calendar page.

outcomes.note: 185 dated sittings across two tenants (115 Corona de Tucson, 70 Sonoita-Elgin), plus 10 directors with contact detail. Both bodies previously held zero meetings and zero roster rows.

routes.title: BoardBook Premier serves an entire meeting archive on one unpaginated page, and its Minutes path is a client-rendered shell

applicability.note: TWO FACTS, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE TRAP. /Public/Organization/{id} returns the ENTIRE archive on one page with no pagination — read 2026-08-29 on meetings.boardbook.org for Pima County JTED No. 11, yielding 267 meetings spanning 2009-2026 with agendas as HTML — and /Public/DownloadAgenda/{slug}?meeting={id} returned a verified 12.4 MB packet PDF. robots.txt answers HTTP 404, so NO_ROBOTS: the host publishes no restriction. THE TRAP: /Public/Minutes/ is a CLIENT-RENDERED shell that strips to 757 bytes of chrome. A parser pointed at it returns nothing and, unless the zero is treated as a failed extraction (RULING 100), reports every meeting in the archive as having empty minutes — an absence manufactured from a rendering choice. The minutes are reachable through the packet and through the 302 on /Documents/FileViewerOrPublic/, neither of which was walked. BoardBook is operated by Sparq Data Solutions Inc. and its market is school districts and JTEDs nationally.

outcomes.note: 267 meetings 2009-2026 with agendas as HTML and packets as PDF, for a body that held zero. The Minutes path yielded 757 bytes of chrome and is recorded as a failed extraction, never as absent minutes.

routes.title: the www host answers 403 to every client while the apex answers 200 and serves the whole site

applicability.note: A HOST IS AN ORIGIN, NOT A GOVERNMENT, AND THE TWO FORMS ARE TWO ORIGINS. Read 2026-08-29: www.pimajted.org answers HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare interstitial titled 'Just a moment...' to four clients, while the apex pimajted.org answers 200, carries robots.txt with 'Disallow: /wp-admin/' only, and serves the entire site including a 267-meeting archive. A session that resolved the www form, met the interstitial and stopped would have recorded a body covering 36 of 44 sampled ZIP points as BLOCKED_CURRENTLY. Under RULING 182 the 403 is TRANSPORT and permission on that origin is CANNOT_TELL; it is never a permission verdict and never a fact about the body. THE GENERAL RULE: try both the apex and the www form before recording any host-level disposition, and record the disposition against the ORIGIN that produced it rather than against the government.

outcomes.note: One body recovered from an apparent block: Pima County JTED No. 11, whose whole archive sits behind the apex while the www form is Cloudflare-gated.

routes.origin: conceived 2026-08-29 when the JTED's published URL carried the www form and answered 403. The apex was tried because RULING 182 requires varying the client and the route before converting a refusal into a verdict, and the origin turned out to be the variable that mattered rather than the client.

claims.statement: The apex and www forms of a hostname are separate origins that can differ in both robots policy and bot gating; a disposition belongs to the origin that produced it.

routes.title: a district moved to a .gov and the government layer that published its URL still names the dead host

applicability.note: AN AUTHORITATIVE GOVERNMENT SOURCE CAN CARRY A DEAD HOST, AND A TLS ERROR CAN BE A TRUE READING OF A HOST THAT STOPPED BEING THE PUBLISHER. Two instances on 2026-08-29. www.mescalj6fd.com was recorded 2026-08-27 as CANNOT_TELL, 'unwalkable because of a certificate' (ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID); the TLS failure is real and reproducible, and plain HTTP answers 200 and redirects to https://mescalj6fd.gov/. www.rinconvalleyfd.org — the URL published by PIMA COUNTY'S OWN fire-taxation GIS layer, which is as authoritative as a source gets for district identity — 404s its robots and redirects to rinconvalleyfdaz.gov. Both districts had been recorded with zero rosters and zero meetings; both publish rosters, agendas and minutes at the new host. THE GENERAL RULE: before recording a body as unreachable, re-resolve its host over plain HTTP and follow redirects, and treat a special district's .com or .org as a candidate for a .gov migration. The corollary is sharper: a URL inherited from an authoritative layer is EVIDENCE, not a fact, and it goes stale like any other observation.

outcomes.note: Two districts recovered: Mescal-J6 (5 directors with term dates) and Rincon Valley (5 directors, agendas AND minutes as first-party PDFs). Both were previously recorded unreachable.

routes.origin: conceived 2026-08-29 working two fire districts the corpus had recorded as unwalkable. Both were expected to be genuine walls and both were stale addresses, which is why the entry is about the CLASS rather than about either district.

claims.statement: A government's own GIS or taxation layer can publish a superseded host for a district; re-resolving over plain HTTP and following redirects reaches the current .gov.
An ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID on a district's old domain can be a stale redirector rather than a broken publisher; it is never evidence about the body.

routes.title: candidate filings and measure texts live with the filing OFFICER, and one county has more than one

applicability.note: A COUNTY'S ELECTIONS DEPARTMENT IS NOT THE ONLY FILING OFFICER, AND 'THE COUNTY HAS PUBLISHED ALMOST NOTHING' CAN BE TRUE OF ONE OFFICE AND FALSE OF ANOTHER. The corpus recorded that the Nov 3 2026 general had exactly ONE published document on the Pima County elections page. That reading was correct about the ELECTIONS DEPARTMENT and wrong as a statement about the county: on 2026-08-29 the Pima County School Superintendent at www.schools.pima.gov published every school district in the county with seats, minimum signatures, and each candidate's name, filing date and signature count — Vail Unified, 2 seats, Andrea Black (filed 2026-07-01, 474 signatures) and Edward Buster (2026-07-02, 374) — plus two ballot measures whose texts extracted from PDFs on pima-county-schools.s3.amazonaws.com. THE CUSTODIAN SPLIT, which is the portable half: FIRE DISTRICTS file with the County Elections Department while SCHOOL DISTRICTS file with the County School Superintendent, so a single 'who do I file with' answer is wrong for one of them. Its robots.txt answers HTTP 200 with a ZERO-BYTE body — a robots that exists and forbids nothing — and the bare host is ECONNREFUSED over HTTPS while the www form serves.

outcomes.note: Two filed candidates with dates and signature counts, and two ballot measures with texts extracted from PDF, for a general election the corpus recorded as having one published document.

routes.title: the publisher's own single-page app names every public route it calls, and one of them answers where the known one does not

applicability.note: A 401 ON THE ONE ROUTE ANYBODY KNOWS IS NOT THE PUBLICATION'S ANSWER. Pima County's campaign-finance filing BODIES answer HTTP 401 at documents/getdocumentfiling/{id} to every client tried — bare curl, a browser user agent, Origin and Referer set, and the trailing-slash form the app itself calls. A prior session correctly recorded that as a wall on a route rather than a statement about the filing, and stopped. On 2026-08-29 the app's own JavaScript bundle was read and all 59 API routes enumerated from it (RULING 207: one route failing never bounds the route universe). /advancedsearch/contributions/{customerId} answers 500 rather than 401, and the ASP.NET stack trace NAMES the cause — ContributionsSearch calling CurrentUserOrWebSiteUserAsync then GetSubdomain(url) throwing on a null URI. The API has its own anonymous WEBSITE-USER path and needed only the tenant subdomain, which it reads from the Origin header. With Origin set it answers HTTP 200 at 1,090,303 bytes: 900 contribution rows and 584 distribution rows, with no credential, no login and no bypass — the identical request the county's own public app makes. THE PORTABLE METHOD: when a known endpoint refuses, read the SPA bundle for the route table before concluding anything, and read a 500's stack trace as a description of what the server wanted rather than as a failure. THE PORTABLE CAUTION: 900 was proved not to be a cap by partitioning against the server (2025: 502 = 502, 2026: 368 = 368), because a truncated result cannot partition consistently.

outcomes.note: 900 contribution rows and 584 distribution rows for Pima County committees, from a record class that had zero rows and a route recorded as walled. Every filing remains a _Redacted public copy and all rows are DocumentType CCFR, so no independent-expenditure row is present and its absence is OURS.

routes.origin: conceived 2026-08-29 under RULING 205, which forbids a route disposition from closing a record obligation. The 401 had already been recorded honestly and the obligation left open; this is what working it rather than accepting it produced.

effort.note: Reading a bundle is a one-off per vendor and yields the whole route table at once. Far cheaper than probing paths, and it finds routes no amount of guessing would.

claims.statement: A publisher's single-page app bundle enumerates the public API routes it calls, and reading it bounds the route universe far better than probing paths does.
An EasyVote campaign-finance API resolves its tenant from the Origin header and serves an anonymous website-user path; a 500 naming GetSubdomain is the server asking for that header, not a refusal.

routes.title: robots.txt answered 403 to our identified client and 200 to a bare one, so the permission question was answerable all along

applicability.note: THE MISTAKE THIS PREVENTS IS RECORDING A PERMISSION QUESTION AS UNANSWERABLE WHEN ONLY OUR CLIENT WAS REFUSED. Under RULING 148 an unanswered permission question refuses the walk, so a robots.txt that 403s does not merely delay a route — it closes the whole fact class behind it. cfs.sos.nh.gov and www.sos.nh.gov were both recorded that way on 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-26. MEASURED 2026-08-31: https://www.sos.nh.gov/robots.txt answers HTTP 200 (2103 bytes, a standard Drupal file) to a bare node fetch, and HTTP 403 to the identical request whose User-Agent carries this project's name. Every Disallow in it is a CMS internal (/core/, /profiles/, /admin/, /user/login, /search/, README files); NOTHING disallows elections, campaign finance or the lobbyist registry. THE PROCEDURE: before recording a permission question as UNANSWERED, re-read robots.txt with the identification REMOVED from the User-Agent and carried in From: and X-Purpose: instead. This is the identified-agent-refused finding applied to the permission read itself rather than to the data fetch, and it is the read that gates everything else. SECOND FINDING, recorded so it is not misread later: cfs.sos.nh.gov publishes no robots.txt — it returns its Angular shell for /robots.txt byte-identically to a nonsense path. That is an absence of published restrictions, NOT a 200 that grants permission; a SPA catch-all is not a rule.

outcomes.note: Permission ANSWERED for both NH SOS hosts: www.sos.nh.gov publishes a robots.txt that forbids no civic path, and cfs.sos.nh.gov publishes none at all. The walk that RULING 148 had refused is permitted.

claims.statement: Re-reading robots.txt with the project's identification moved out of the User-Agent and into From:/X-Purpose: is a route that can answer a permission question previously recorded as unanswerable.

routes.title: a live-browser procedure whose only browser-shaped part was CORS is a server-side script

applicability.note: THE MISTAKE THIS PREVENTS IS RECORDING A ROUTE AS HUMAN-ONLY BECAUSE IT WAS DISCOVERED IN A BROWSER. The NH CFS route was recorded on 2026-08-21 as: open the app in a VISIBLE browser, read its own JS bundles for endpoints, and call cfsapi.sos.nh.gov/api FROM THE PAGE'S OWN CONTEXT 'where CORS is already allowed'. Tracker NH40 concluded it was 'a procedure and not a script, so nothing in CI can repeat it'. MEASURED 2026-08-31: CORS is enforced by BROWSERS, not by servers. A plain server-side POST to https://cfsapi.sos.nh.gov/api/PublicFilerDetails/GetFilingEntityDetails carrying Origin and Referer headers answers HTTP 200 with JSON, no browser and no session. THE PROCEDURE: when a working route requires a live browser, name WHAT THE BROWSER SUPPLIED. If it supplied CORS relief, an Origin/Referer header, or a same-origin context, a server can send those headers and the procedure becomes a script. If it supplied JavaScript rendering of the data, an authenticated session, or a challenge response, it cannot, and the human-only record stands. The distinction is worth making explicitly because the two look identical in a session report and only one of them can be put in CI.
